ruled_out_vectors.description: FullMath.mulDiv / mulDivRoundingUp phantom overflow or precision loss
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: Craft inputs (a, b, denominator) to mulDiv such that intermediate 512-bit product overflows or result is off by more than 1 unit, enabling attacker to extract tokens via price miscalculation.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: mulDiv uses Knuth Vol.2 phantom-overflow-free 512-bit intermediate math. mulDivRoundingUp verified >= mulDiv for all fuzz inputs. No overflow path reachable from valid pool inputs. Forge test covers max uint256 inputs.

ruled_out_vectors.description: FixedPool swapByInput profitable round-trip via rounding exploitation
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: Exploit rounding direction in FixedHelper.swapByInput / _calculateInputLPAndProtocolFee: if output rounds up instead of down, attacker swaps A→B→A and receives more A than deposited.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: calculateFixedSwapByRatioRoundingDown uses mulDiv (round down) for output computation — favors pool. _calculateInputLPAndProtocolFee uses mulDivRoundingUp for fee — favors pool. Round-trip produces strictly <= initial amount. Forge fuzz confirms no profit path.

ruled_out_vectors.description: FixedPool swapByOutput profitable round-trip via output-path rounding
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: In swapByOutput path, calculateFixedSwapByRatio uses mulDivRoundingUp for input required. If combined with fee path, attacker may receive output while paying less input than AMM math requires.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: calculateFixedSwapByRatio (output path) uses mulDivRoundingUp — rounds input UP (favors pool). _calculateOutputLPAndProtocolFee uses mulDivRoundingUp(reserveAmountIn, poolFeeBPS, MAX_BPS - poolFeeBPS) — also rounds up. No output-path underpayment possible. swapByInput fallback check (L917) reverts if amountIn would exceed initialAmountIn. Forge confirmed.

ruled_out_vectors.description: DynamicPool tick-crossing arithmetic: free token creation via SwapMath.computeSwapStep
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: Craft swap crossing exact tick boundary such that amountOut > amountIn (after fee), extracting tokens from the pool through AMM price-step arithmetic error.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: SwapMath.computeSwapStep ensures amountOut <= computed from price change (SqrtPriceMath rounds in protocol's favor). Forge test: exact tick boundary step, single-tick range. Medusa MedusaDynamicMath property_amount0DeltaRounding and property_amount1DeltaRounding (4/4) confirm rounding direction. No free token creation.

ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: _splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight has a Slither-flagged uninitialized local variable (returnableInput). If it retains stale data from a prior call, amountInFilledByInputHeight could be subtracted by a nonzero amount, returning more input to the caller than they provided.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: Solidity 0-initializes all local variables. returnableInput = 0 by default. Only increased (never reduced) within the function. The path where returnableInput remains 0 causes amountInFilledByInputHeight -= 0 (no change). Integration tests confirm no value creation. Slither false positive.

ruled_out_vectors.description: snapPrice free price manipulation: skip initialized ticks via liquidityChange=0
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: Call DynamicPoolType.snapPrice with liquidityChange=0 and targetSqrtPriceX96 far from current price. If tick bitmap guard is not enforced, attacker can set price to arbitrary value without swapping, then drain LP positions via one-sided arbitrage.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: DynamicHelper.snapPrice traverses tick bitmap between current and target price. Any initialized tick triggers revert DynamicPool__PriceCannotSnapWithLiquidity. Cannot skip LP position ranges. Forge test in H_R4_CP02_SnapPriceBoundary.t.sol confirms boundary enforcement.

ruled_out_vectors.description: directSwap pricing bounds bypass: afterSwap receives 0 as beforeSwap amount for input-based swaps
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: AMMStandardHook.beforeSwap stores params.amount in transient storage. For input-based directSwap, params.amount=0 at beforeSwap time. afterSwap reads 0, computes computeRatioX96(0, amount) = MAX_SQRT_RATIO or MIN_SQRT_RATIO — always within bounds regardless of actual price. Allows unlimited price movement in a directSwap.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: This is known pattern HOOK-001/CP-004, documented in CLAUDE.md. directSwap requires pre-approved transfer; the hook design intentionally allows LP-controlled pricing bounds. The pricing bounds check validates post-swap price against hook-configured bounds, not against a price oracle. Not a novel exploit path — attacker must already control the hook to benefit.

ruled_out_vectors.description: SingleProvider hook extreme price return: price=0 or price=type(uint256).max drains pool
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: Deploy mock hook to SingleProviderPoolType returning price=0 or price=MAX_UINT. If the pool type does not bound-check the hook's return value, swap calculations collapse and LP liquidity is drained.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: SingleProviderPoolType: only allowedProvider (returned by hook) can add liquidity. Hook IS the LP by design — market maker model. Hook returning extreme prices harms only itself (its own LP position). No permissionless drain path. SingleProviderHelper calculateFixedInput/calculateFixedOutput use mulDiv which returns 0 for price=0 inputs — swap returns 0 output, no drain.

ruled_out_vectors.description: Flash loan + DynamicPool: single-block price manipulation for LP drain
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: Use flash loan to acquire large token position, swing DynamicPool price far from market, drain LP liquidity at off-market price, repay flash loan. Net profit if price swing arbitrage exceeds flash loan fee.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: DynamicPool price only moves via swaps bounded by Uniswap v3 AMM math. Each swap step respects constant-product invariant per tick. No free price manipulation outside of swaps. Flash loan attack is equivalent to a large swap which itself is bounded — LP receives proportional fee. Forge test: no profitable round-trip on DynamicPool across 10k fuzz iterations.

ruled_out_vectors.description: Cetus-pattern: crafted tick_index → computeRatioX96 overflow → near-zero price → LP drain
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: Cetus ($223M exploit): tick_index was not bounds-checked, causing getSqrtRatioAtTick to overflow, yielding near-zero price. Attacker deposits minimal token0, receives massive token1. Check if LimitBreak TickMath has equivalent unchecked tick_index path.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick reverts for tick < MIN_TICK or tick > MAX_TICK (boundary guards at function entry). computeRatioX96 handles zero amounts by returning 0 for both-zero inputs, MAX_SQRT_RATIO for one-zero. Forge C14 tests: round-trip at every 1000th tick from MIN_TICK to MAX_TICK — all pass. Forge C19 tests: both-zero, one-zero, overflow-to-zero cases verified. No Cetus-equivalent path.

ruled_out_vectors.description: BitMath assembly De Bruijn incorrect-shift: wrong MSB/LSB causes mispriced tick lookup
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: Slither flags BitMath.mostSignificantBit / leastSignificantBit as incorrect-shift. If the De Bruijn lookup table shift is wrong, getTickAtSqrtPrice returns wrong tick, causing DynamicPool to cross ticks at wrong prices and enabling LP drain.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: Solady LibBit De Bruijn MSB/LSB implementation is a well-audited pattern. Slither cannot parse complex assembly lookup table patterns — known FP. Forge C15 test: MSB/LSB for all 256 powers of 2 (0..255), plus MSB(0) revert, MSB(1)==0, MSB(uint256.max)==255. All pass. Not a vulnerability.

ruled_out_vectors.description: Balancer-pattern: wrong rounding direction in FixedHelper — sequential dust swaps drain pool balance
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: If any division in FixedHelper._calculateAmountOut, _calculateAmountIn, addLiquidity, or removeLiquidity rounds in the user's favor rather than the protocol's, then 1000 sequential 1-wei swaps reduce pool balance, constituting a slow drain.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: All output computations in FixedHelper use mulDiv (round DOWN for output). All fee computations use mulDivRoundingUp (round UP for fee = round DOWN for net output). _addLiquidity / _removeLiquidity: add then remove X difference <= 1 wei per operation (Forge C6 fuzz). Medusa MedusaFixedMath property_noRoundTripProfit (7/7 properties, 50k iterations). Pool balance never decreases from 1-wei swaps.

ruled_out_vectors.description: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput double-roundup: attacker extracts value via +2 wei overpayment
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput applies two sequential mulDivRoundingUp calls. Each can round up by 1 unit. Net: input calculated as up to +2 wei more than mathematically required. Could a maker/taker exploit this for profit?
ruled_out_vectors.reason: The +2 wei per call is from MAKER to PROTOCOL — rounding is against the maker, not the taker. Attacker cannot extract value; they can only cause themselves to overpay by ≤2 wei. This is dust (well below gas cost). No profit extraction path for any party.

ruled_out_vectors.description: FeeHelper output-swap unchecked subtraction underflow: protocolFeeAmount > feeAmount
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: In _calculateBPSFeeWithRecipientAndProtocolFeeSwapByOutput, an unchecked block computes feeAmount -= protocolFeeAmount. If protocolFeeBPS could exceed MAX_BPS (10,000), protocolFeeAmount > feeAmount → underflow → massive feeAmount returned → attacker receives overly large fee disbursement.
ruled_out_vectors.reason: feeAmount = mulDivRoundingUp(inputAmount, exchangeFeeBPS, MAX_BPS - exchangeFeeBPS). protocolFeeAmount = mulDivRoundingUp(feeAmount, protocolFeeBPS, MAX_BPS). Since protocolFeeBPS <= MAX_BPS (enforced by pool creation validation), protocolFeeAmount <= feeAmount always. Unchecked subtraction is safe. C29 analysis confirms.

ruled_out_vectors.description: First depositor inflation attack on SingleProviderPoolType or DynamicPoolType share accounting
ruled_out_vectors.attack_hypothesis: ERC-4626 pattern: first LP deposits 1 wei, donates large amount to contract, second LP gets 0 shares due to rounding inflation. Apply to DynamicPoolType (liquidity shares) and SingleProviderPoolType (LP position).
ruled_out_vectors.reason: DynamicPoolType uses Uniswap v3-style liquidity units — not share-ratio accounting. Liquidity is computed from (amount0, amount1, sqrtPrice) via SqrtPriceMath, not from totalSupply/totalAssets. No share inflation possible. SingleProviderPoolType: only allowedProvider can add liquidity (access-controlled entry point). No permissionless second depositor to exploit. ERC-4626 pattern is N/A for both pool types.

false_positives.reason: Solady LibBit De Bruijn MSB/LSB implementation. Slither cannot parse complex assembly lookup table patterns. All 2^0..2^255 inputs verified correct in C15 Forge tests.

_finalizeSwapCollectFundsAndDisburse is protected by nonReentrantWithFlags. The ETH refund call to executor occurs before the balance check, but any reentrant call would be blocked by the transient storage flag. Cross-swap exploitation is impossible since swap state is fully committed before any external call.

nativeValueUsed0 is a local boolean in memory — immutable to external calls. Slither incorrectly flags memory locals as stale after external calls. The logic correctly OR's both native-value-used flags.

Diamond proxy pattern via DelegateCall.delegateCallPure. The assembly return(0, size) returns the delegatecall returndata to the original caller. Slither cannot model cross-function delegatecall returns.
FixedPoolType.pools and FixedPoolType.positions are storage mappings — default-initialized to empty (zero values). Populated at runtime through createPool/addLiquidity. Not a vulnerability.

Intentional precision alignment. currentHeight0 / precision0 * precision0 rounds down startHeight to the nearest precision boundary. Required for correct height-map linked-list alignment. The 1-unit truncation is a design invariant, not a precision bug.
setTokenSettings is guarded by nonReentrant. External call to tokenHook.hookFlags() is at the beginning before state writes. Reentrancy cannot bypass the single-entry guard.

false_positives.description: snapPrice free price manipulation via liquidityChange=0
false_positives.reason: DynamicHelper.snapPrice reverts with DynamicPool__PriceCannotSnapWithLiquidity if any initialized tick exists between current and target price (tick bitmap traversal check). Cannot snap through LP position ranges.

false_positives.description: directSwap pricing bounds bypass via zero beforeSwap amount (HOOK-001/CP-004)
false_positives.reason: For input-based directSwap, amountIn is 0 at beforeSwap time. AMMStandardHook stores 0 in DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT, causing afterSwap to compute MAX_SQRT_RATIO or MIN_SQRT_RATIO — always within bounds. This is CP-004 / HOOK-001 (documented in codebase). Previously analyzed and not novel.

false_positives.description: SingleProvider pool hook price manipulation — hook returns attacker-favorable price
false_positives.reason: In SingleProviderPoolType, the pool hook IS the LP (market maker). The hook is the price oracle by design. Only allowedProvider (from hook) can add liquidity. Market maker model: LP accepts risk of adverse selection in exchange for spread capture.

The _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) call intentionally clears flags to allow hook fee transfers after swap finalization. By this point, all input collection, output disbursement, and pool state updates are complete. A reentrant second swap would operate on correctly-updated state. No double-spend possible.

false_positives.description: feeOnTop not included in permit SWAP_TYPEHASH signature
false_positives.reason: SWAP_TYPEHASH omits feeOnTop fields. Executor can specify arbitrary feeOnTop. Protected by: (1) for input swaps — revert if feeOnTop > amountIn; (2) for output swaps — user's limitAmount slippage check catches excessive total input. By-design for executor-controlled fee model. Previously noted in CLAUDE.md.
